sources.citation: Quinault Indian Nation. 2025. Quinault Dictionary (Webonary/SIL online dictionary, built from Ruth Modrow's Quinault Dictionary re-spelled in the 2007 QIN orthography). Pages: Alphabet, Phonology, Grammar, Introduction, Foreword, Entries explained, Browse Quinault-English.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement: the 'Phonology' and 'Grammar' pages are unfilled template placeholders. Entries do carry per-word stress marks in a syllabified pronunciation field (e.g. ɑ́ɑ.cɑn 'bow of a canoe', ɑ.cɪ́t.x̣oɫ 'stiff', ɑl.tɑ́m 'everything', ɑ.mɑ.tɑ́m 'something', ɑp̓.ʔɑ́ 'Comeback salmon'), i.e. stress is marked lexically and falls on varying syllables, but no rule is given.

sources.citation: Terry-itewaste, Cosette Lelani. 2016. Quinault Language Revitalization: Bridging Linguistic Theory to Community Classrooms. PhD dissertation, University of Arizona (hdl 10150/621357), 94 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.4.1 'Phonology of Quinault' (pp. 27-28) gives only a 7-vowel chart and a 27-consonant chart (summarizing Modrow); the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the dissertation. Its reference list names Gibson 1964 'Quinault Phonemics' (UW MA thesis), Modrow 1969 Quinault Dictionary / Conversational Quinault, and Rowicka 2006 IJAL.

sources.citation: Kinkade, M. Dale. 1993. The Non-Lexical Basis for a Tsamosan Branch of Salish. Papers for the 28th International Conference on Salish and Neighboring Languages, pp. 175-203 (UBCWPL Kinkade Collection).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Quinault: p.177 'More Quinault data exist, although only the phonology has had anything like adequate analysis, making it necessary to leave Quinault out of discussion at this time.' Stress remarks (unstressed-vowel deletion, stressed-vowel lengthening, single primary stress in compounds) are stated for Upper Chehalis/Cowlitz only; sec. 4 notes a short/long vowel contrast in all four Tsamosan languages.
